what: The declared role of every archived measurement row. fitcheck.calibrate reads this file, not a glob, so a repeat, a hold-out or a legacy row cannot wander into a fit. Roles: 'calibration' (fitted), 'holdout' (scored, never fitted), 'repeat' (a re-run of a config already declared), 'excluded' (unusable, with a reason).

roles.calibration: fitted by `python -m fitcheck.calibrate`; every shipped coefficient traces back to these rows
roles.holdout: never fitted; scored with --role holdout --check to grade the shipped constants out of sample
roles.repeat: a re-measurement of a config already present under another run_id; kept as evidence, never fitted
roles.excluded: cannot be used, for the reason on the row

t4-2026-09-01.emitted_by: transcribed from fitcheck.ipynb cell outputs; predates measure.py --json

known_gaps: The 12-row out-of-sample hold-out quoted in docs/SPEC.md was produced by fitcheck.ipynb (VALIDATION 1-4) and written to validation.zip inside the Kaggle session. That archive was never committed, so no row here carries role 'holdout'. Until it is re-run and archived, the hold-out figures in the docs are historical and are labelled as such.
